summary.plain: XMASS was a detector holding 832 kg of liquid xenon in the Kamioka mine in Japan, built to look for dark matter by watching for its faint flashes of light. It ran from 2013 to 2019, saw no dark matter, and set limits on several kinds of dark matter.
summary.technical: Single-phase liquid xenon scintillation detector: 642 PMTs viewing 835 kg of xenon in a copper vessel, inside a 72-PMT water-Cherenkov muon veto, at 2700 m.w.e. Stable data taking Nov 2013 - Feb 2019 (1590.9 live days); 97 kg fiducial volume. Full-dataset WIMP-nucleon limit 1.4e-44 cm^2 at 60 GeV/c^2; annual-modulation, Migdal and bremsstrahlung searches for lighter WIMPs.

technology.quote: 642 inward-facing photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) in an approximate spherical shape in a copper vessel filled with pure liquid xenon
technology.value: Single-phase liquid xenon scintillation detector viewed by 642 photomultiplier tubes
